question.text: Ganga Credit Opportunities Fund II (Cat II AIF) has a Total Committed Capital of INR 300 crore. The PPM fixes Management Fees at 2.00% p.a. (excluding GST of 18%) charged on Committed Capital during the commitment period. For Year 1, what is the TOTAL CASH OUTFLOW of the fund towards Management Fees, including GST?

explanation.text: The Logic: Base fee = 2.00% x INR 300 crore = INR 6.00 crore. GST @ 18% on INR 6.00 crore = INR 1.08 crore. Total outflow = INR 6.00 + INR 1.08 = INR 7.08 crore. The chapter's Example 6.1/6.2 follows this exact pattern: fee x committed capital, then gross-up with GST at 18%. The Trap: A stops before adding GST; C applies 18% as a deduction instead of addition (INR 6.00 x 0.90 is a common trap); D mis-computes GST at ~9% (confuses GST on some other service category). Cross-Exam Context: Same arithmetic appears in XIX-C. PMS (XXI-B) uses similar GST-on-management-fee mechanics but on portfolio AUM, not committed capital. Manager's Pro-Tip: AIFs generally cannot recover GST as input tax credit because the fund does not provide taxable output services. Build this as sunk cost in the LP's net-return model — otherwise you'll over-quote the net IRR by roughly 36-54 bps at a 2% fee.
